items.headline: Federal judge pauses discovery in Amazon's lawsuit against Perplexity
items.summary: A federal court stayed discovery in Amazon's case against Perplexity over its agentic AI shopping tool Comet, days after an appeals court lifted an earlier injunction that had barred the tool from Amazon.com. The dispute is an early test of how courts will treat AI agents that act on a user's behalf on third-party websites.

items.headline: US tightens AI chip export rules to close China's overseas data-center loophole
items.summary: The Trump administration moved to block Chinese firms from indirectly accessing advanced American AI chips and models through data centers in third countries, with lawmakers also pushing tougher legislation. The move extends a broader, ongoing US effort to restrict China's access to frontier AI hardware.

items.headline: Anthropic commits $3.4 billion to gas generators for AI data centers
items.summary: Anthropic agreed to pay roughly $3.4 billion for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty Caterpillar gas generators, taking over orders, engineering and construction from supplier OnePWR Solutions. It's described as the largest known single purchase of power-generation equipment by an AI lab, underscoring how electricity supply is becoming a bottleneck for AI buildouts.

items.headline: Meta's infrastructure chief Santosh Janardhan to step down
items.summary: Janardhan, who led Meta's infrastructure organization and co-headed engineering for roughly 17 years, told staff he will leave in early 2027; former AWS executive Dave Brown will take over infrastructure. The shift comes as Meta plans $135-145 billion in capital spending this year, much of it on AI data centers.

items.headline: Wall Street tech selloff deepens on AI spending and export-curb worries
items.summary: US technology and semiconductor stocks fell sharply ahead of Nvidia's quarterly results, as investors weighed new US restrictions on AI chip exports to China alongside broader concern about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending.

items.headline: Mistral launches Large 4 ('Le Chonk') and expands Studio for enterprise AI agents
items.summary: French AI lab Mistral introduced its Large 4 model, aimed at coding, defensive cybersecurity and document reasoning, alongside an expanded Studio platform for building and deploying managed agents, workflows and apps across cloud, VPC or on-premises environments.

items.headline: Swiss startup Embodied AI unveils AIR, a cageless wheeled factory robot
items.summary: Embodied AI debuted AIR at Humanoid Europe 2026 in Munich: a wheeled, two-armed robot with soft, compliant arms designed to work alongside factory staff without a safety cage, and to learn new tasks from human demonstration within about a month. It reflects a broader industry push toward humanoid-style robots that can be deployed safely in existing factories.

items.headline: OpenAI and Cisco use AI to hunt and help patch Linux kernel vulnerabilities
items.summary: Through OpenAI's Daybreak cybersecurity program, a cyber-focused model automatically searched for Linux kernel flaws, tested exploitability and suggested fixes, with human researchers reviewing findings before disclosure to maintainers. Cisco is a partner in the effort, which signals growing use of frontier AI for large-scale vulnerability discovery.

items.headline: Analysis: most AI models released in 2026 are open-weight
items.summary: A BenchLeader analysis found that open-weight models account for about 56% of new AI model releases with known licenses in 2026, even though proprietary models still dominate the very top of performance rankings. It's a data point in the ongoing debate over whether open or closed models will define the AI ecosystem.

items.headline: AWS open-sources Strands Decider 2B, a fast lightweight decision model
items.summary: Amazon's Strands Labs released an open-source model built on Alibaba's Qwen3.5-2B base that answers from a fixed set of options with a confidence score instead of generating free text, aimed at low-latency agentic decision-making. AWS positions it as a cheaper, open-weight alternative to hosted decision-model APIs like Jev.
